analysis.investment_thesis: Can Fin Homes is growing net profit at 22.1% CAGR while trading at P/E 11.87 — that's a PEG ratio of 0.54, one of the most attractively priced growth stories I've seen in Indian financials. Affordable housing finance for first-time homebuyers is a sector tailwind you can see just by walking around any Tier-2 Indian city.
key_strengths: Exceptional GARP profile: P/E 11.87 against 22.1% profit CAGR delivers PEG of 0.54 — the kind of number that makes me reach for my checkbook
ROE of 16.92% with Forward P/E of 10.49, meaning the market is pricing in deceleration that hasn't shown up in the numbers yet
Canara Bank promoter backing (29.99%) provides funding access and credibility — lowers cost of borrowings compared to standalone HFCs
key_risks: Finance costs growing at 29.3% CAGR vs revenue at 18.8% — borrowing costs are outpacing income growth, compressing net interest margins over time
D/E of 6.59 is normal for HFCs but leaves the business exposed to systemic credit market disruptions or rising rates
Only 3 years of data available — hard to assess through-cycle performance; OCF was deeply negative in 2022-23 as the loan book expanded rapidly
red_flags: Finance cost CAGR of 29.3% significantly exceeds revenue CAGR of 18.8% — if this trend persists, margin compression will eventually pressure net profit growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
When I see a financial services company growing profits at 22% and trading at P/E 12, I ask: what's the catch? For Can Fin Homes, the main concern is the squeeze between borrowing costs (rising fast at 29.3% CAGR) and lending income (18.8% CAGR) — this NIM compression is real and worth watching. But the company is still delivering robust profit growth (857 Cr in FY25 vs 471 Cr in FY22), and with total assets growing from 27,944 Cr to 40,967 Cr over 3 years, the loan book expansion is healthy.

The affordable housing segment in India has enormous runway — government schemes like PMAY, urbanization, and a young working-age population with rising incomes are all structural tailwinds. Can Fin Homes, with its PSB parent backing and conservative lending to salaried first-time buyers, is well-positioned to compound in this environment. At a PEG of 0.54 with Forward P/E of 10.49, the market is pricing in risk that doesn't appear imminent. I'd buy in tranches and monitor the NIM trend closely.
